prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core theme: “Secure future” by sticking to the current economic plan, cutting taxes, controlling immigration, strengthening defence, and reforming public services while keeping net zero pragmatic and affordable.

Economy and tax
- Maintain fiscal rules with debt falling; cut waste and shrink the civil service to pre‑pandemic size.
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament; no rises to income tax or VAT.
- Triple Lock Plus: both State Pension and a new age‑related tax‑free allowance rise by inflation/earnings/2.5%.
- Childcare: 30 free hours from 9 months to school; move Child Benefit to a household test (tapering £120k–£160k).
- Clamp down on tax avoidance/evasion (£6bn a year by end of Parliament).
- Back business: keep corporation tax rate; maintain/extend full expensing (including leasing when affordable); 10‑point SME plan; £36bn HS2 savings to local transport; nationwide gigabit/5G; accelerate planning; £22bn public R&D, AI compute, advanced manufacturing; financial services/City reforms; new trade deals (India, GCC), leverage CPTPP; regulatory reform using Brexit freedoms.

Work, welfare and skills
- Reform disability benefits (PIP) and Work Capability Assessment to focus support on greatest need and improve mental health provision.
- Overhaul fit notes (specialist work/health sign‑off); tougher sanctions with 12‑month claimant review; expand UC rollout; new Fraud Bill.
- Education: mandatory National Service at 18 (military placements or civic service); 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by closing poor‑value degrees; Advanced British Standard for 16–19; mobile phone bans in schools; parental transparency on sensitive content.

Borders and migration
- Legal, annually shrinking cap on work/family visas with annual Commons vote.
- Higher salary thresholds, pre‑travel health checks and higher IHS; end student discount; integration focus.
- Illegal migration: monthly Rwanda flights from July; implement Illegal Migration Act; crack down on smugglers; rewrite asylum rules; new returns deals.

NHS and social care
- NHS spending rises above inflation; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors.
- Pharmacy First expansion; 250 GP surgeries modernised/built; 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres.
- Dental Recovery Plan (2.5m appointments), service commitment for new dentists.
- £3.4bn tech upgrade (NHS App front door, AI, scan reading, data platform); cut managers by 5,500; expand mental health support (schools coverage to 100% by 2030, early support hubs).

Law, order and communities
- 8,000 more neighbourhood police; hotspot policing; Martyn’s Law; tougher sentences for serious crime, VAWG, knife crime; four new prisons; stronger protest controls; new extremism definition applied.
- Levelling up: towns endowments, Community Ownership Fund, more Freeports/Investment Zones; extend £2 bus fare for full Parliament.
- Backing Drivers Bill: ban road pricing by councils/Mayors; reverse London ULEZ expansion; local referendums for 20mph/LTNs.

Housing
- 1.6m homes: fast‑track brownfield, densify cities (esp. London), abolish nutrient neutrality (with mitigation) to unlock 100k homes; protect Green Belt.
- New Help to Buy; permanent FTB SDLT threshold £425k; renters reform (abolish Section 21 after court changes); complete leasehold reform; CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants; local/UK connection tests for social housing.

Energy, net zero and environment
- Net zero 2050 with lower household levies; annual North Sea licensing; new gas plants; treble offshore wind; two SMR fleets approved in 100 days; Wylfa new plant; CCS clusters; import carbon pricing by 2027; no fracking; onshore wind with consent; solar on rooftops/brownfield; home efficiency vouchers; maintain price cap, PumpWatch.
- Flood defence funding maintained; Plan for Water (tougher penalties, exec bonus bans for serious breaches); tree/peat funding; new National Park; tougher waste crime; limit new incinerators.

Defence and foreign policy
- Defence to 2.5% of GDP by 2030 (fully funded); £10bn munitions; at least 5% of defence budget to R&D; long‑term support for Ukraine; Veterans’ Bill and enhanced benefits.
- Development: return to 0.7% when fiscal tests met; national‑interest test; climate finance maintained.

Union, rural, farming and fisheries
- Protect UK internal market; more levelling up funds in Scotland, Wales, NI; specific energy/transport commitments.
- Farming budget up £1bn over Parliament; legal food security target; fast‑track farm infrastructure; extend Seafood Fund with focus on inshore fleet.

Equality, sex and gender
- Clarify Equality Act: sex means biological sex; protect single‑sex spaces and women’s sport; implement Cass Review; school guidance on gender questioning.
